8201.full: 1. white-rump , the name of a kind of antelope, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. the white-tailed eagle, the erne , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. (ML)

8210.full: 1. a man's pack, baggage , αὐτόφορτος οἰκείᾳ σαγῇ, i. e. carrying his own baggage, (Aeschulus Tragicus): generally, harness, equipment , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. = σάγμα II, a pack-saddle , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

8218.full: σεμνότης, -ητος, ἡ (σεμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:12 * ;] gravity: 1Ti.2:2 3:4 (Vg. eastitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, see word), Tit.2:7.† (AS)

s: the trunk of an old olive-tree
8221.full: 1. a pen, fold , for lambs, kids, calves, (Homer); ς. δράκοντος the dragon's den , (Euripides) 2. a sacred enclosure, chapel, shrine , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. a sepulchre, burial-place , (Simonides Lyricus) 4. the trunk of an old olive-tree , (Lysias Orator) (ML)

8222.full: σημειόω, -ῶ (σημεῖον), [in LXX: Psa.4:6 (נָשָׂא)* ;] to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: 2Th.3:14 (frequently in π.; see ICC, M, Th., in l).† (AS)

8225.full: 1. to have strength or might, be strong or mighty , (Sophocles Tragicus); σθ. χερί, ποσί to be strong in hand, in foot, (Sophocles Tragicus); σθένοντος ἐν πλούτῳ (Sophocles Tragicus); τοσοῦτον σθένει (Sophocles Tragicus); ὅσονπερ ἂν σθένῃ (Sophocles Tragicus); οἱ κάτω σθένοντες they who have power below, (Euripides) 2. with infinitive to have strength or power to do, be able , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

8233.full: 1. grain, corn: food made from grain, bread , ποιεῖσθαι σιτία ἀπὸ ὀλυρέων to feed off spelt, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. generally, food, victuals, provisions , (Herdotus Historicus); σιτία ἡμερῶν τριῶν three days' provision , of soldiers, (Aristophanes Comicus); σιτία καὶ ποτά meat and drink, (Plato Philosophus) 3. τἀν Πρυτανείῳ σιτία public maintenance in the Prytaneum, (Aristophanes Comicus); compare σίτησις. 4. rarely food for dogs, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

8234.full: 1. silence , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; σιωπὴν ποιεῖν (Xenophon Historicus); ἦν ς. there was a hush or calm , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. the habit of silence , (Demosthenes Orator) 3. dative σιωπῇ as adverb, in silence , (Homer), attic derivation uncertain (ML)

8245.full: crookedness , (Plutarch): in plural the windings of a stream, etc., (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

8249.full: look on as dung, reject contemptuously

8256.full: σκύβαλον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Sir.27:4 * ;] refuse, esp. dung (see MM, ii, iii, xxiii): Php.3:8.† (AS)

8257.full: σκῆνος, -ους, τό [in LXX: Wis.9:15 * ;] = σκηνή, a tent, tabernacle (C.1., 3071). Metaphorical, of the body as the tabernacle of the soul: 2Co.5:1 5:4.† (AS)

s: one who is clever in matters of life, a wise man
8261.full: 1. a master of one's craft or art, an adept , of a diviner, (Herdotus Historicus); of poets, (Pindar); of the Creator, (Plato Philosophus); metaphorically, ς. πημάτων an adept in misery, (Euripides) 2. like φρόνιμος, one who is clever in matters of life, a wise man , in which sense the seven Sages are called σοφισταί, (Herdotus Historicus); of Prometheus, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. at Athens, a Sophist , i. e. a professor of grammar, rhetoric, politics, mathematics, such as Prodicus, Gorgias, Protagoras, (Thucydides), etc. At first the Sophists were held in honour; but from their loose principles they fell into ill repute, and the word came to mean, 4. a sophist (in bad sense), a quibbler, cheat , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

8267.full: σπιλόω [in LXX: Wis.15:4 * ;] to stain, spot, defile: with accusative, Jas.3:6, Ju 23.† (AS)

s: hence, to feel pity or compassion
8269.full: σπλαγχνίζομαι (σπλάγχνον), [in LXX (act., -ίζω): Pro.17:5 A, 2Ma.6:8 (= -εύω) * ;] to be moved as to the σπλάγχνα (which see), hence, to feel pity or compassion: absol., Luk.10:33 15:20; ptcp., σπλαγχνισθείς, with indic., Mat.18:27 20:34, Mrk.1:41; before ἐπί, with dative of person(s), Mat.14:14, Luk.7:13; ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.15:32, Mrk.6:34 8:2 9:22; ωερί, Mat.9:36. (The word is elsewhere found only in Sm: 1Ki.23:21, Eze.24:21, Test. Zeb., 4:6-7; see Thayer, see word; MM, xxiii quote Thumb, Hellen., 123 as practically confirming Lft. on Php.1:8, in the suggestion that the verb was a coinage of the Jewish dispersion.) † (AS)

8270.full: Pass. to be burnt to ashes , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

8272.full: σπουδαίως adv. (σπουδαῖος), [in LXX: Wis.2:6 * ;] __1. with haste or zeal, i.e. earnestly, zealously, diligently: Luk.7:4, 2Ti.1:17, Tit.3:13; compar., -οτέρως, Php.2:28 (RV, Lft., Weymouth, al., but see infr.) __2. hastily, speedily: compar., -οτέρως, Php.2:28 (Thayer, Zorell, see word; ICC, in l, al., but see supr.).† (AS)

s: in haste; hence, zealous, eager, diligent, earnest
8273.full: σπουδαῖος, -α, -ον (σπουδή), [in LXX: Eze.41:25 * ;] in haste; hence, zealous, eager, diligent, earnest: before ἐν, 2Co.8:22; compar., -οτεροσς 2Co.8:17 (here in superl. sense, see Bl., § 44, 3) 2Co.8:22.† (AS)

8274.full: 1. rare, scarce, scanty , (Herdotus Historicus); σπάνιον ἑαυτὸν παρέχειν, Lat. difficiles aditus habere, (Plato Philosophus); ὕδατι σπανίῳ χρώμενοι having a scanty supply of water, (Thucydides); with infinitive, σπ. ἰδεῖν rare to behold, (Xenophon Historicus): of persons in an adverb sense, σπάνιος ἐπιφοιτᾷ he seldom visits, (Herdotus Historicus):—; σπάνιόν ἐστι, with infinitive, it is seldom that . ., (Xenophon Historicus):—; τὸ σπάνιον = σπάνις, (Aeschines Orator) 2. comparative σπανιώτερος, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Sup. -ώτατος, attic 3. adverb -ίως, seldom , (Xenophon Historicus); so σπανίᾳ, (Plato Philosophus): comparative -ιώτερον, (Thucydides) (ML)

8275.full: scarcity, rareness, dearth, lack of a thing, (Euripides):—; οὐ σπάνις [ ἐστι] = οὐ σπάνιον, there is no lack , no difficulty , (Euripides) (ML)

8284.full: 1. waterproof , (Herdotus Historicus); στεγνὰ οἰκήματα, of a cave, (Euripides) 2. as Substantive, στεγνόν, οῦ, a covered dwelling , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

8286.full: 1. to be mourned, giving cause for grief , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. mournful , (Euripides) (ML)

8288.full: to deprive of a thing, (Thucydides):—;Pass. to be deprived of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), attic (ML)

8291.full: Mid. or Pass. to paint one's eyelids and eyebrows with black paint στίβι); (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

8292.full: punctured , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;generally, spotted, dappled , (Sophocles Tragicus); στικτὰ ὄμματα, of the hundred eyes of Argus, (Euripides) (ML)

s: in late writers, to walk by rule
8295.full: στοιχέω, -ῶ (στοῖχος, a row), [in LXX: Ecc.11:6 (כָּשֵׁר) * ;] to be in rows (of waves, plants, etc., as well as of men), to walk in line (esp. of marching in file to battle; Xen., Cyr., vi, 3, 34, al.). Metaphorical, in late writers, to walk by rule: Act.21:24; with dative, to walk by or in (as a rule of life), Rom.4:12 (cf. MM, xxiii), Gal.5:25 6:16, Php.3:16 (cf. συν-στοιχέω).† (AS)

8296.full: 1. to set a row of poles with nets to drive the game into, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to order or arrange in system , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)
